ethiopian.title: Churches of Ethiopia
ethiopian.description: Churches from across the country, with their history, location and living traditions.

items.name: Bete Giyorgis
items.description: A cross-shaped church carved down into solid rock in the 13th century, the most celebrated of the Lalibela churches.

items.name: Church of Our Lady Mary of Zion
items.description: The most sacred church in Ethiopian Orthodox tradition, said to house the Ark of the Covenant.

items.name: Debre Damo Monastery
items.description: A 6th-century monastery on a flat-topped mountain, reached only by climbing a leather rope.

items.name: Abuna Yemata Guh
items.description: A cliff-face church with ancient paintings, reached by a steep climb up the rock.

items.name: Debre Berhan Selassie
items.description: A 17th-century church famous for its ceiling painted with rows of angel faces.

items.name: Ura Kidane Mehret
items.description: A monastery church on Lake Tana with richly painted interior walls.

items.name: Debre Libanos Monastery
items.description: A 13th-century monastery founded by Abuna Tekle Haymanot, one of the great centres of Ethiopian Christianity.

items.name: Holy Trinity Cathedral
items.description: The capital's principal cathedral, completed in 1941 and the resting place of Emperor Haile Selassie.
